description: A TypeScript client for trip planning, stop departures, and single-trip lookups over the Spider transit API — one typed client that ships the allowed queries and attaches auth for you, with zero runtime dependencies.
rules: Construct one client with `new SpiderClient(baseUrl, apiKey)`, where `baseUrl` is the per-environment host `https://your-env-slug.api.tiducto.eu` and the key is sent in an `apikey` header scoped to a single project and environment. All three surfaces — `client.routing`, `client.stops`, `client.realtime` — are ready immediately; there is no install step. Use the literal placeholders `your-env-slug` and `your-api-key` in examples.

Plan a trip with `client.routing.plan({ origin, destination, first })`, building each endpoint via `Location.coordinate(lat, lon)` or `Location.stop(id)`. Page results with `planNext`/`planPrevious` (or stream pages with `planUntil`); other routing calls are `departures(...)` for a stop's upcoming departures and `trip(tripId)` for a single trip's stops and times.

Every call returns a `SpiderResult<T>`, a discriminated union on `isSuccess` — branch on it, then read `data` or `error` instead of relying on exceptions. `error.code` is one of network, timeout, unauthorized, not_found, server, rate_limited, decoding, unknown. Only a contract-version mismatch throws, as `SpiderContractMismatchError`.

`client.stops` offers text/autocomplete `search`, lookup by GTFS id via `byId`, and geo queries `near(lat, lng)` / `within(bbox)`. `client.realtime` is poll-based with no push connections — call `vehicles`, `vehicleForTrip`, `delays`, or `alerts` on an interval and read `freshness` on each snapshot.
